comments.author: @workingTchr
comments.text: While a provisional patent can't be extended once its year runs out, you COULD file a new one at the end of that year, and if your invention has not yet been publicly disclosed, you have another year to work with, right?

comments.author: @miinimarble
comments.text:
Hot take: you can file a U.S. provisional pro se, sure. But in practice, strong provisionals are usually drafted/filed with a patent attorney. Why? Priority only sticks if the disclosure actually enables the invention. Thin write-ups get picked apart when you convert or go foreign. Startups sometimes roll the dice to save cash, but if you want solid figures, embodiments/variants, and parameter ranges, professional help is necessary.

Bonus: a good practitioner often expands your ideas and embodiments while drafting :)
